minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved an 8% budget and rate increase, five sewer bylaw changes, and the town meeting articles.
minutes.summary: Final meeting for the outgoing DPW director/engineer Rob Oliva. The commission accepted the FY23 sewer budget with an eight percent increase and set new rates, approved the CTS contract year-three increase, voted on five sewer bylaw changes headed to annual town meeting, approved the town meeting articles, a consultant scope for the SSO notification plan, the Q3 commitment, and minutes. ARPA project priorities were discussed and a new assistant to the business manager was announced.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to accept the FY23 sewer budget with an eight percent increase, by roll call with all members aye as heard.
The commission then voted to enact a new sewer rate, minimum charge and wells charge, effective for 1/22 as heard.
Five sewer bylaw changes were approved section by section, and the commission voted to send the sewer articles to the annual town meeting warrant.
The commission accepted a consultant scope for the SSO notification plan and approved the third quarter commitment.
The vote on year three of the CTS contract was not audible in the recording, so the outcome is not established.

why_it_matters: Sewer rates and the minimum charge set here flow into sewer bills for customers on the system, and the town meeting articles are votes residents will be asked to take.

The bylaw changes and the SSO notification plan govern how the sewer system is regulated and what the commission must report to DEP, and ARPA priorities such as pump station rehab could mean large capital costs.
watch_next: Annual town meeting vote on the sewer bylaw changes and the FY23 budget, capital reserve and OPEB articles.
Finance Committee presentation on March 24, with Zoom or in-person format still to be worked out.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on nearly every vote and on most figures, and the differences are mostly caption errors in names, dates and dollar amounts. The one thing to check is the CTS/CTE year-3 contract vote, which our record could not hear but the town records as passed 5-0, along with the Section 4.0 vote, which the two describe differently.
